tasks.short: Turn pay and benefits research into a clear report or guide for managers and employees.

today.trigger: An annual reward review or a policy change creates a need to publish compensation and benefits findings.
steps: Agree the audience, publication format and questions with the HR Director.
Collect approved AFAS extracts, Power BI figures, relevant CAO clauses and external research.
Reconcile figures in Excel and check which findings apply across sites, shifts and employee groups.
Write the report or guide in Word and prepare supporting charts or slides.
Obtain factual and policy review, then publish the approved version in SharePoint.
drudgery: Copying figures between spreadsheets, charts and documents.
Rewriting technical findings for different audiences.
today.time_sinks: The supplied baseline is 16 hours a year. Source reconciliation, drafting and review take most of the effort; waiting for reviewers can dominate elapsed time.

lenses.faster: Draft from an approved evidence pack, with charts linked to checked Excel tables. Manual copying, first-draft writing and repeated formatting largely disappear.
lenses.autonomous: An approved evidence pack can trigger a draft and a list of missing references. Publication stays with the specialist after factual and policy review.
lenses.ambitious: Produce a manager briefing, an employee guide and a shift-friendly one-page summary from the same findings. Explain how benefits work for different employee groups without exposing individual pay.
lenses.joy: Remove reference formatting, repetitive rewriting and document assembly. Keep the work of explaining trade-offs and making reward policies understandable.
lenses.options: Generate several outlines and explanations of the same finding, including plain English and Dutch versions. Compare readability and likely misunderstandings before choosing.
lenses.altitude: Own the publication standard, evidence requirements and review process. Improve reusable templates and checks instead of rebuilding each report.
reach: Prepare checked reward explanations for HR Business Partners.
Supply recruiters with approved benefits wording.
Prepare compensation research summaries for the HR Director and Controller.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist judges whether findings are fair, locally relevant and consistent with the applicable CAO, and whether wording could create an unintended promise. The HR Director retains policy decisions, with OR involvement where legally required.
tasks.pattern_why: AI can structure and rewrite supplied research, but this low-volume task depends on interpreting compensation evidence and explaining sensitive findings. Use deterministic checks for numbers and references; keep conclusions and publication under human control.

in_practice.trigger: The specialist marks a source pack as ready for drafting in SharePoint.
steps: Assemble dated, approved sources and aggregated tables, identifying the applicable CAO and employee groups.
Validate totals, denominators, reporting periods and small-group disclosure rules using Excel checks.
Use an approved enterprise AI service to draft the chosen publication, linking factual claims to supplied sources and flagging unsupported statements.
Generate audience variants and check every figure, reference, translation and policy statement against the source pack.
Resolve reviewer comments and publish the approved document in SharePoint.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist verifies evidence and interpretation; the HR Director approves policy wording and any external publication. Confirm whether the proposed policy requires OR advice or consent before presenting it as decided.
systems: Approved enterprise AI service, subject to availability and access controls
data_needed: Aggregated pay and benefits figures with definitions and reporting dates.
Current CAO clauses and approved company policies.
External research with publication dates, usage rights and source references.
Approved terminology, publication templates and audience requirements.
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint publication folder containing the source register, checked tables, draft versions, review decisions and final approval; exclude unnecessary employee-level data.

evidence.claim: Language models can turn supplied research into draft reports and audience-specific summaries, but claims and references need human verification.
Excel checks and linked charts can reduce manual reconciliation and copying in recurring publications.
A 45% reduction in total task time is a planning estimate, assuming a usable source pack and unchanged review waiting time; it has not been measured at Noordhaven.

risks: AI may invent references, misstate study findings or apply an outdated CAO clause.
Pay comparisons may mix contracted hours, overtime, shift allowances or different employee populations.
Small groups can reveal individual compensation even when names are removed; apply AVG/GDPR data minimisation and access restrictions.
Draft wording can imply a benefit entitlement or policy commitment that has not been approved.
Report drafting alone does not establish an EU AI Act high-risk use; reassess requirements if the workflow expands into individual pay, promotion or other employment decisions.
research_questions: What publications did this task produce last year, and how much of the 16 hours went to drafting versus evidence checks and approval?
Can approved aggregate figures be reproduced from AFAS and Power BI with consistent definitions across sites and CAOs?
Which enterprise AI service is approved for compensation research, and what data may it process?
In a trial using the last publication, does the workflow reduce total time while preserving every checked figure, source and policy meaning?

role.altitude: Become the owner of reliable reward evidence and clear compensation communication, setting standards for how research supports pay and benefits decisions.
reach: Provide HR Business Partners with reusable reward briefings.
Maintain approved benefits explanations for recruitment and onboarding.
Support the Controller with documented assumptions behind reward proposals.
Help the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst define consistent compensation measures.
role.ceiling_note: This task accounts for only 16 hours a year. At the estimated 45% saving, it releases about 7.2 hours, worth EUR 540 in capacity at EUR 75 per hour, rather than a cash saving; broader role gains require examining other tasks.
skills_to_grow: Checking research quality, references and compensation comparisons.
Building reproducible Excel checks and interpreting Power BI measures.
Writing clear Dutch reward explanations for office and shift workers.
Applying CAO, OR and privacy requirements to reward publications.
Evaluating AI drafts and managing approved source packs.
role.ambitious_version: Maintain a shared, checked reward evidence base that produces timely explanations for employees, managers and recruiters. Use feedback to improve understanding of pay and benefits, and test whether clearer expectations support offer acceptance and 90-day retention.
